title: Add batching tier selection examples + migration guide from manual batching knobs
text:
Add batching tier selection examples + migration guide from manual batching knobs

body:
Summary: This PR adds end-to-end examples for selecting the new workload-aware batching SLO tiers (fast / standard / cost-efficient) and a migration guide for customers moving off manual batching knobs (max_batch_tokens, max_wait_ms, etc.) to tier defaults. The goal is to reduce support churn during rollout and make the recommended path obvious for Hosted API users while also documenting Dedicated override precedence at a high level.

Context: Runtime 1.22 introduces tiered batching defaults with reason codes and policy precedence (customer override > route policy > tier default). Customers currently using manual batching config have asked for a practical mapping and a safe migration sequence that preserves tail latency (especially streaming). This PR updates examples to match the new SDK/API surface (tier selection via request param or header) and adds troubleshooting notes for common pitfalls seen in canary.

What’s included: (1) Python example: choose tier per request (and per route) with streaming vs non-streaming variants; shows how to log the effective tier and selection reason codes returned in response metadata. (2) TypeScript example: configure tier at client construction + override per call; includes a simple concurrency harness to compare p95 latency across tiers. (3) Migration guide: recommended steps to remove manual batching knobs, validate with a small traffic slice, and what to watch in metrics (queue depth, batch size distribution, p99 for fast). (4) Dedicated note: how precedence works when tenant-level overrides are set.

Non-goals: This does not document full scheduler internals or perf methodology; it references the official docs/benchmarks for detailed numbers. It also does not add new product behavior—examples only.

Testing: Ran examples against staging (hosted) with tiered defaults enabled; validated streaming fast-tier example maintains stable first-token latency and that metadata fields render in logs. CI passes.

Follow-ups: Once public docs PR lands, we should link the migration guide from the docs site and de-duplicate sections (tracked in ENG-18432).

review_conversation:
Henry Cho: Can we be explicit about default behavior if customers do nothing? Also call out that tier selection is optional and route policy may override request-level in some orgs.
Wei Chen (author): Added a short section in the migration guide: default is standard tier unless route policy pins otherwise; request-level tier is only honored when allowed by policy (link to policy precedence note).
Lena Fischer: The fast-tier example should emphasize streaming stability and avoiding large prompt bursts; can we add a note about concurrency? Also the reason code names should match runtime telemetry (TIER_DEFAULT, CUSTOMER_OVERRIDE, OVERLOAD_MODE).
Wei Chen (author): Updated fast-tier README with a concurrency warning + suggested max in-flight per worker; aligned reason code strings with runtime naming and added a small table of common codes.
Chloe Martin: In Dedicated section, please avoid implying customers can set per-request tier if their admin policy disallows it. Suggest phrasing: 'may be restricted by org policy'.
Wei Chen (author): Adjusted wording and added a callout box: 'Your org may restrict request-level tier selection; check Console route policy'.
Elliot Price: Migration guide is solid. Please add one short 'roll back' step: re-enable previous manual knobs or pin tier to standard if fast regresses. Also add a link placeholder for public docs (to be updated post-merge).
Wei Chen (author): Added rollback steps + link placeholder to docs site; we can update URLs once the public docs PR merges.
